# Tasks Document

Tasks are listed in a **topological order** consistent with the DAG below; linear document order does not imply serial execution. This is deliberately the **smallest** of the recent specs — there is no new build-time machinery, so the task graph is shallow. Three independent shared-edit branches can run in parallel, and the **content/doc prerequisites** (Tasks 4–6) are sequenced to land **with or before** the route rewires so the tree is never red-by-construction (design → *Implementation sequencing*).

```mermaid
graph TD
    T1[1: Velite updated field] --> T6[6: seed MDX content]
    T1 --> T8[8: /now route]
    T2[2: format-date UTC + test] --> T8
    T3[3: siteConfig.slashPages + test] --> T10[10: /sitemap]
    T3 --> T11[11: /slashes]
    T4[4: authoring doc] --> T5[5: check-authoring-docs parameterize + test]
    T6 --> T7[7: /about flip indexable]
    T6 --> T8
    T6 --> T9[9: /colophon route]
    T6 --> T14[14: seed-sentinel test]
    T6 --> T15[15: now updated date-only test]
    T7 --> T16[16: E2E suite]
    T8 --> T16
    T9 --> T16
    T10 --> T16
    T11 --> T16
    T13[13: footer links] --> T16
    T12[12: XML sitemap removal]
```

## Revision history

- **v1**: Initial decomposition of the approved v4 design (post-r3 adversarial on both requirements and design). The design verified every pinned mechanism against live code and converged on a no-new-machinery shape, so the tasks pin the design's load-bearing decisions rather than inventing structure: (a) the Velite change is a **field addition only** (`updated: s.isodate().optional()`), no transform edit (Task 1, Req 4.1); (b) the date fix is **central** in `formatContentDate` (`timeZone: "UTC"`) with a single TZ-independent-by-construction assertion (Task 2, Req 2.2/10.4); (c) the **content/doc prerequisites are in-spec, gated deliverables** sequenced before/with the route edits so no gate is red-by-construction mid-spec (Tasks 4–6, design *Implementation sequencing*); (d) `getNowPage()` is the entry-existence throw **plus** an `updated`-presence throw, while `getColophonPage()` mirrors `getAboutPage()` exactly (Tasks 8, 9, Req 2.3/3.2); (e) the `!/T/` date-only assertion rides the Req 10.3 seed test as the load-bearing CI gate against the UTC display-shift (Task 15); (f) the authoring-doc check is **parameterized over a doc-list** and its self-test is updated per the design's literal diff spec — the three pure-core call-sites, the per-doc `writeDocs` helper, and the per-doc zero-byte count (Task 5, Req 9.3); (g) the `/sitemap`/`/slashes` pages read `siteConfig` + `src/lib` helpers and never `src/app/sitemap.ts` (Tasks 10, 11, Req 5.5); (h) the lone XML edit removes the two `noindex` routes (Task 12, Req 7.6). A Requirements Coverage Matrix at the foot makes orphan-AC visibility explicit.
- **v4 (post-r3 adversarial review of tasks.md, FINAL)**: r3 verified the v3 re-fix of the r2 blocker with a **live repro of the exact UTC-CI condition** — `TZ=UTC node`, reassign `process.env.TZ="America/Toronto"` in module scope, then dynamic-import the formatter → renders "May 28" on the un-fixed formatter, so the standing `=== "May 29, 2026"` assertion now genuinely goes red in CI if `timeZone:"UTC"` is reverted. r3 also confirmed `format-date.ts` imports nothing (so the dedicated file's dynamic import has no transitive `format-date` chain), `vitest.config.ts` has no `setupFiles` and no `isolate:false` (clean per-file registry), Task 5's inlined self-test is internally consistent with `main(AUTHORING_DOCS)`, and the DAG/ordering/coverage are intact — declaring the document **converged / implementation-ready** and explicitly declining to manufacture a fourth structural objection. One **cosmetic** Novel finding, accepted: v3 mis-grouped `THEME_STORAGE_KEY` with the local copy-idiom helpers, but it is `export const` in `src/components/layout/theme-provider.tsx` and is imported by the sibling axe suites. v4 corrects Task 16 to **import** `THEME_STORAGE_KEY` and copy only the three genuinely-local helpers (`setupTheme`/`assertTheme`/`AXE_TAGS`). No other change — the prior rounds' decisions stand.
- **v3 (post-r2 adversarial review of tasks.md)**: r2 attacked the v2 deltas against live code and found that the headline v2 fix was **inert** — one blocker, plus two nicks; all accepted. (1) **(BLOCKER) Task 2's TZ-pinned regression guard did not work in the file it targeted.** `src/lib/format-date.test.ts:3` static-imports `formatContentDate` (and `:4-5` re-import it via `blog`/`projects`), so the module-level `contentDateFormatter` constant is constructed under the runner's **ambient** zone at file load — *before* any test sets `process.env.TZ`. The prescribed `await import("./format-date")` is then a registry cache hit (same module record) and does **not** reconstruct the formatter under the pinned zone; and the one standard escape, `vi.resetModules()`, is **explicitly forbidden** by `format-date.test.ts:1` ("parity assertions depend on shared module instances"). Net: in a UTC CI box the guard stays green on the broken *and* fixed formatter — exactly the hole v2 claimed to close. v3 moves the guard into a **dedicated new file `src/lib/format-date-tz.test.ts`** with **no static `format-date` import**, setting `process.env.TZ = "America/Toronto"` at the top *before* the lone dynamic `import`; per-file vitest isolation (no `isolate:false` in `vitest.config.ts`) gives that file a clean module registry, so the formatter constructs under the pinned zone and the assertion goes red on the un-fixed formatter (renders "May 28"). The zone math itself was verified correct. (2) **(minor) Task 5's inlined checklist left `SUBJECT_REL`/`subjectHeadings` dangling and under-specified the per-doc warning message** — the production `::warning::` line currently hardcodes the contributions path but must become **per-doc** under `main(AUTHORING_DOCS)`, and the self-test only matched `/::warning::/` so a wrong path would pass silently. v3 defines the identifiers inline and adds a restriction that the warning includes the doc's `rel` path and the self-test asserts the *correct* doc path. (3) **(cosmetic) Task 16's `_Leverage` overstated reuse** — `AXE_TAGS`/`setupTheme`/`assertTheme` are local, non-exported in `blog-axe.test.ts`/`contact-axe.test.ts`, so the new suite **copies the idiom**, it does not import it; v3 fixes the phrasing. r2 re-verified the DAG, dependency edges, red-by-construction sequencing, the axe scope (warranted; `@axe-core/playwright@^4.11.3` already installed, so no new dep/edge), the coupling note, and every static citation as correct — no structural change in v3.
- **v2 (post-r1 adversarial review of tasks.md)**: r1 verified every citation against live code (found no stale reference or ordering bug) and surfaced three significant precision gaps plus two polish items — all accepted. (1) **Task 2's UTC test did not *guard* the regression in a UTC CI runner** — `formatContentDate("2026-05-29T00:00:00.000Z") === "May 29, 2026"` is green on *both* the broken and fixed formatter when the runner's `TZ` is UTC, so a future revert of `timeZone: "UTC"` would pass CI silently. v2 makes Task 2's test **pin `TZ` to a west-of-UTC zone (`America/Toronto`) and dynamically import `formatContentDate` after** so the module-level formatter constructs under that zone — the assertion then goes red on the un-fixed formatter (renders "May 28"). This is a deliberate, minimal TZ harness and **supersedes the v1/design "no TZ harness needed, true by construction" framing**, which conflated *correctness verification* with *regression protection* (r1 Finding 1, Conclusion 1). (2) **Task 16 omitted the axe/WCAG E2E pass that every sibling page-type ships** (`blog-axe`/`contact-axe`/`projects-*` run `AxeBuilder` per page per theme); for five new pages (three indexable) that is thinner than the cross-spec accessibility convention the NFRs themselves call blocking. v2 adds an `AxeBuilder` pass to Task 16 (r1 Finding 2, Conclusion 3). (3) **Task 5 deferred its four hardest edits to the design's "literal diff spec"** rather than inlining them, breaking task self-containment for a fresh-context implementer; v2 **inlines the four-item checklist verbatim** into Task 5 (r1 Finding 3). (4) **Task 6's `Success:` under-covered its colophon deliverable**; v2 strengthens it to require a real stack-documenting body with no sentinel, and Task 14 (already reading all three files) covers colophon emptiness (r1 Finding 4). (5) Polish: an explicit note that route-tasks 7/9/11 have soft `Success:` halves backstopped by Task 16 — a conscious coupling, not an independent gate (r1 Finding 5); and Task 14's self-contradictory `File:` line is fixed (r1 cosmetic). r1 confirmed the DAG is complete, the dependency edges honest, and the topological order genuinely prevents a red-by-construction "done" state — no structural change in v2.

---

## `_Requirements:` footer semantics

Each task's `_Requirements:` footer lists the requirement IDs it **contributes to satisfying** (in whole or in part) — not the requirements it transitively depends on. A requirement may be covered by several tasks; the Requirements Coverage Matrix at the document foot gives the inverse mapping so orphan requirements are visible at review time. All `_Prompt` fields are written for a fresh-context implementer and begin with the spec-workflow re-entry instruction.

**Route-task ↔ E2E coupling (v2, conscious).** The route-wiring tasks (7, 9, 11) have `Success:` halves — `/about` reporting `index: true`, `/colophon` rendering the stack body, `/slashes` listing all six — whose *mechanical* proof lives in **Task 16** (the E2E capstone) and the **Task 3** invariant test, not in the route task itself. This is deliberate: the route tasks are thin wiring, and concentrating the runtime proofs in the E2E suite avoids brittle per-route render harnesses. The coupling is recorded here so Task 16 is never descoped on the assumption that 7/9/11 are independently gated — they are not. Note also AC 1.2 (the `getAboutPage()` build-time guard) is **verify-only with no automated regression guard** — the design consciously declines a missing-entry test to avoid destabilizing the shared `pages` collection; the module-load throw is the live safeguard, and this is an accepted trade, not an oversight.

The formatter is a **module-level constant** constructed once at import, so the zone must be set **before** the module loads. It **cannot** live in the existing `src/lib/format-date.test.ts`: that file (line 3) static-imports `formatContentDate` (and lines 4-5 re-import it via `blog`/`projects`), so the formatter is already constructed under the ambient zone at file load — a later `await import` is a cache hit and `vi.resetModules()` is explicitly forbidden there (line 1: "parity assertions depend on shared module instances"). Per-file vitest isolation (no `isolate:false` in `vitest.config.ts`) gives this file a clean module registry, so the formatter constructs under `America/Toronto`: the un-fixed (no-`timeZone`) formatter renders "May 28, 2026" → red; the fixed UTC formatter renders "May 29, 2026" → green. Leave `format-date.test.ts` untouched (its loose-regex cases stay green). This **supersedes the design's "no TZ harness / true by construction" note** (which proved correctness post-fix but did not guard a future revert).

  - _Leverage: src/lib/format-date.ts (single formatter, 1-9); src/lib/format-date.test.ts (existing cases — leave intact); vitest per-file isolation + dynamic-import + `process.env.TZ` pattern_

- [ ] 5. Parameterize the authoring-doc check over a doc-list and update its self-test
  - File: scripts/check-authoring-docs.mjs, scripts/check-authoring-docs.test.mjs
  - **Script (`check-authoring-docs.mjs`) edits:** export `SLASH_PAGES_HEADINGS` (the four Task-4 headings) and `AUTHORING_DOCS` (`[{ path, headings }]` for contributions + slash-pages); keep `CANONICAL_HEADINGS` exported (contributions set); change `checkHeadings(docText, headings)` to take the headings list; make `main(docs)` **iterate all docs, aggregate the exit code, and report every problem** — it does NOT `process.exit` on the first missing doc (it `continue`s and exits once after the loop). Preserve per-doc semantics: doc-not-found → exit-non-zero + stderr + NO annotation; missing heading → `::warning::` + exit-non-zero. **(v3) The `::warning::` line must name the offending doc's own `rel` path** (per-doc — interpolate the current `rel`, not the hardcoded contributions path the single-doc script used), so two docs can't emit indistinguishable warnings. The CLI entrypoint calls `main(AUTHORING_DOCS)`.
  - **Self-test (`check-authoring-docs.test.mjs`) — the four inlined edits (v2: stated verbatim so the task is self-contained; no need to open design.md):**
    1. *Pure-core call-sites (3 edits).* The three existing one-arg calls now pass the headings list explicitly: `checkHeadings(ALL_PRESENT, CANONICAL_HEADINGS)`, `checkHeadings(CANONICAL_HEADINGS.slice(1).join("\n\n"), CANONICAL_HEADINGS)`, `checkHeadings("", CANONICAL_HEADINGS)`. (Without the second arg, `headings` is `undefined` and `headings.filter` throws.)
    2. *Per-doc `writeDocs` helper* replaces the single-doc helper + the `ALL_PRESENT = CANONICAL_HEADINGS.join(...)` constant. It writes EVERY `AUTHORING_DOCS` entry, defaulting each to its OWN `headings.join("\n\n")`, and derives each doc's dir from its `rel` via `path.dirname` (so it generalizes beyond `docs/`):
       ```js
       function writeDocs(dir, overrides = {}) {
         for (const { path: rel, headings } of AUTHORING_DOCS) {
           const content = rel in overrides ? overrides[rel] : headings.join("\n\n");
           const abs = path.join(dir, rel);
           mkdirSync(path.dirname(abs), { recursive: true });
           writeFileSync(abs, content);
         }
       }
       ```
    3. *The four CLI assertions* (run against `main()`'s report-all behavior). Pick the slash-pages doc as the subject, defining inline at the top of the test: `const SUBJECT_REL = "docs/slash-pages-authoring.md"` and `const subjectHeadings = SLASH_PAGES_HEADINGS` (both imported from the script). Then: all-present (`writeDocs(dir, {})`) → exit 0, no `::warning::`; one heading missing in the subject doc (`writeDocs(dir, { [SUBJECT_REL]: subjectHeadings.slice(1).join("\n\n") })`, sibling full-present) → exit non-zero + a `::warning::` **whose text contains `SUBJECT_REL`** (proving the per-doc message, not just `/::warning::/`); **neither** doc written (`makeTmp()` only, no `writeDocs`) → exit non-zero + **two** `author doc not found` stderr lines + NO `::warning::`; zero-byte subject doc (sibling full-present) → exit non-zero + `warningCount === subjectHeadings.length` (i.e. `SLASH_PAGES_HEADINGS.length` — **NOT** the hardcoded `CANONICAL_HEADINGS.length`/9 from the current `test.mjs:104`).
    4. *Exports the test imports*: `CANONICAL_HEADINGS` stays exported (existing import unchanged); `SLASH_PAGES_HEADINGS` and `AUTHORING_DOCS` are new imports.
  - Purpose: gate the new doc for heading-drift with the same machinery as the sibling, no new CI script (Req 9.3).
  - _Leverage: scripts/check-authoring-docs.mjs (pure `checkHeadings` core, `::warning::` form); scripts/check-authoring-docs.test.mjs; design "CI authoring-doc check" literal diff spec_
  - _Requirements: 9.3_
  - _Depends on: 4 (the doc must exist so the production `AUTHORING_DOCS` entry passes)_

Everything you need is in this task — no need to open design.md. Mark in-progress before starting; log-implementation when done, then mark complete. | Restrictions: Keep `CANONICAL_HEADINGS` exported (existing import); `main()` reports ALL docs (no early exit); the `::warning::` message must interpolate the per-doc `rel` (not a hardcoded path) and the self-test must assert the warning contains `SUBJECT_REL`; do NOT hardcode the zero-byte count to 9; no new CI script. | _Leverage: scripts/check-authoring-docs.mjs + .test.mjs | _Requirements: 9.3 | Success: `node --test scripts/check-authoring-docs.test.mjs` passes; `pnpm check:authoring-docs` exits 0 with both docs present; a removed heading in either doc fails it._
